result.summary: Adds `btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target` and related constants to the libbitcoinkernel C API, C++ wrapper, and kernel internals. This allows kernel consumers to configure disabled, manual, or automatic pruning targets when initializing a `ChainstateManager`. The function validates target boundary constraints and updates both block manager and chainstate load options.
result.problem: libbitcoinkernel provides no mechanism to set block pruning options on `ChainstateManagerOptions`. Opening an existing pruned datadir in libbitcoinkernel fails during `LoadChainstate()` because the block manager detects prior pruning while chainstate load options default to unpruned mode, requiring a reindex.
evidence: Closes #35627 ('kernel: can't work with pruned blocksdir')

PR description: 'Consequently, trying to open an existing pruned node\'s data directory fails during node::LoadChainstate() with: [error] Failed to load chain state from your data directory: You need to rebuild the database using -reindex to go back to unpruned mode.'
result.card: libbitcoinkernel users cannot configure block pruning, making it impossible to load an existing pruned node data directory without failing chainstate initialization. This PR introduces btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target() and prune target constants to the kernel C API and C++ wrapper. This fixes issue #35627 and allows kernel consumers to initialize and operate on pruned node directories.

risk.why: It only exposes an existing internal option to the libbitcoinkernel C API and does not change node pruning or consensus logic.
